coverage_basis: Sections and physical PDF pages were taken from the full-text cards. W15 entries denote this continuation batch; W16 entries denote full reads already documented in the earlier W16 cards. This file does not upgrade partial or unread records.

sections.id: Front matter and Part I §1, The Discrete Noiseless Channel
sections.coverage: Identifies the July/October corrected reprint and sets up finite-length noiseless coding, allowed symbol sequences, and capacity as asymptotic growth; the finite-state determinant formula is developed in §1 and Appendix 1.

sections.id: Part I §§2–8, Discrete Source of Information; English approximations; Markov and ergodic sources; entropy and source entropy
sections.coverage: Defines finite-state/Markov sources, ergodic versus mixed cases, the entropy axioms and formula, source entropy rate, typical sequences, and entropy approximations. Theorem 3 is the finite-state ergodic source asymptotic equipartition statement; the assumptions and ε/δ quantifiers are retained in the card.

sections.id: Part I §§9–10, Fundamental Theorem for a Noiseless Channel; Discussion and Examples
sections.coverage: Relates source entropy to noiseless-channel capacity and gives asymptotic coding and arithmetic-code arguments, followed by examples and limitations of constructive code search.

sections.id: Part II §§11–17, Discrete Channel with Noise
sections.coverage: Defines noisy discrete channels and equivocation, maximizes mutual information for channel capacity, states and proves the discrete noisy coding theorem by typical-set/random-assignment counting, and treats examples and constrained-capacity cases.
Provides the finite-state sequence-growth determinant argument, entropy-form derivation, ergodic-source typical-sequence proof, and constrained finite-state coding-rate optimization.

sections.id: Part III §§18–23, Mathematical Preliminaries for Function Ensembles
sections.coverage: Defines function ensembles and band limitation; develops differential entropy, coordinate-change Jacobian, entropy power, linear-filter entropy change (Theorem 14), and the independent-sum entropy-power bounds (Theorem 15).

Defines continuous-channel information rate by mutual information, derives the independent additive-noise formula (Theorem 16), average-transmitter-power capacity with constraint P (Theorem 17, physical p. 43), entropy-power bounds for arbitrary noise (Theorem 18), and peak-transmitter-power bounds with S explicitly the peak allowed power (Theorem 20, physical pp. 45–47). The P and S constraints are distinct.

sections.id: Part V §§27–29, Rate for a Continuous Source
sections.coverage: Defines fidelity and rate minimization; states coding feasibility relative to channel capacity (Theorem 21), the white-noise mean-square-error formula (Theorem 22), and general source-rate bounds (Theorem 23).

Reads remaining end matter and derivations, including the continuous-source rate argument and Appendix 7’s measure-theoretic mutual-information definition and data-processing inequality for postprocessing the received signal.
Frames the small-deletion capacity problem, related work, numerical illustration, notation and proof roadmap.

Defines the binary deletion channel and stationary-ergodic information rate; states the finite-block capacity characterization and Lemma 2.2 (subadditivity/variational limit), whose proofs are in Appendix A.

sections.id: Section 3, Intuition behind the main theorem
sections.coverage: Gives an explicitly heuristic derivation of the near-Bernoulli run law and ambiguity correction; it does not prove the quadratic term.

sections.id: Section 4, Proof of the main theorem: Outline
sections.coverage: States the lemmas used for the matching lower/upper bounds and explains the proof dependency.
Proves run-law/entropy, achievability, modified-deletion, super-run, tail, and ambiguity estimates used in Theorem 1.1.
Gives the first-order Markov-source comparison and explicitly asks whether higher coefficients and a convergent small-d series exist; offers only heuristic cluster/correlation reasoning.

sections.id: Appendix A, Proofs of Preliminary Results
sections.coverage: Proves Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.2, including the finite-block superadditivity argument and stationary block construction.

sections.id: Appendix B, Proofs of Lemmas in Section 5.1
sections.coverage: Supplies deferred entropy, run-length, and tail estimates for the first group of Section 5 lemmas.
Introduces the perturbed deletion process and bounds the corresponding conditional-entropy correction.

sections.id: Appendix D, Proof of Lemma 5.23 and its corollaries
sections.coverage: Counts the single-/multiple-parent-run deletion cases and controls the remaining terms to prove the deferred ambiguity estimate.
Lists cited works.
Proves the entropy-scale deletion-channel converse by counting deletion patterns and dirty alignments; takes block length to infinity before the small-deletion limit.
Introduces the i.i.d. deletion/duplication capacity problem and the typical-output/jigsaw coding approach.
Defines the block/type framework and code construction.
Establishes typical-output properties for run-structured inputs.

sections.id: Section III-B, Decoding Error Probability: A Simplified Analysis
sections.coverage: Counts compatible type/block assignments, uses Stirling estimates and atypical-codeword pruning, and bounds decoding error.
Allows deviations in block counts and proves Proposition 1 as a concentration statement for typical-output block counts; it is not an entropy-tail correction.

sections.id: Sections IV–VI, Run-law examples and discussion
sections.coverage: Evaluates geometric and other run distributions and discusses the resulting lower bounds.
Presents the generalized jigsaw/typical-output framework.

sections.id: Section VIII, I.I.D. Channels with Duplications
sections.coverage: Extends the construction to duplication-channel models.
Concludes; technical appendices prove supporting lemmas. Proposition 1 remains the block-count typicality result, not an entropy truncation result.
Surveys trace/subsequence formulations, Markov-input greedy decoding, and jigsaw/run-structured lower bounds.
Derives a Poisson-repeat reduction and a lower bound in the stated deletion model.
Surveys information-theoretic capacity formulations, upper-bound methods, trace reconstruction, and related synchronization variants.
Defines the binary i.i.d. deletion channel and previews genie-aided upper bounds and auxiliary-channel lower bounds.

sections.id: Section II, A Useful Auxiliary Channel
sections.coverage: Defines a finite fixed-block channel with L input bits, R output bits, D=L−R uniformly chosen deletion positions among binom(L,D), independently across channel uses; proves Lemmas 1–9 used later.
Reveals the deletion-related process Z to the decoder and reduces the bound to an auxiliary-channel mutual information.
Uses a second revealed process to derive a computable capacity upper bound.
Reveals process V to encoder and decoder and bounds the resulting channel.
Gives the receiver-only V bound.
Compares numerical bounds, distinguishes proved statements from conjectures, and reports this paper’s C₂*/(1−d)→0.49 high-deletion limit against the prior [7] comparison value 0.7918.

sections.id: Section VIII, Two Simple Lower Bounds
sections.coverage: Derives simple achievable-rate bounds using the auxiliary process.
Concludes and lists references; section boundary shares PDF p. 24.
Introduces the deletion-channel converse problem and the two bound regimes.
Defines run-length notation and capacity-per-unit-cost tools.
Proves a genie/run-length upper bound and a marker-based high-deletion asymptotic using Lemmas 1–4.
Identifies the Harvard Computer Science Technical Report TR-07-04.
States the deletion-channel setting and motivates run-structured achievable-rate constructions.
Presents typical-output error analysis and Theorem 1 statement; explicitly defers Theorem 1 proof to the full version.
Contains a collision-argument sketch, Theorem 2 statement and geometric-run Corollary 1; explicitly defers the detailed Corollary 1 proof to the full version.
Presents report-level discussion and plots, then concludes; no omitted full-version proof is supplied here.
Introduces the small deletion/substitution regime and states the entropy-scale goal.
Defines the binary channel and its deletion/substitution probabilities.
Bounds confusable edit patterns for fixed deletion/substitution counts and proves Theorem 1.
Averages over i.i.d. edit counts to state the small-probability capacity bounds, then summarizes the result.
Lists cited sources.
Positions learned run-law optimization relative to existing deletion-channel lower bounds and states the paper’s contributions.

sections.id: Section II, Model and Renewal Inputs
sections.coverage: Defines stationary renewal inputs, finite-window run deletions, and renewal weights.
Derives the DM functional, renewal reduction, and one-sided truncation; Proposition 1 provides the retained-mass entropy correction.
Decomposes the output/conditional entropy and introduces a residual-state chain to extend the VTR lower bound to finite-support run laws.

sections.id: Section V, Optimization and Verified Evaluation
sections.coverage: Separates search protocols from interval-arithmetic certification at a specified law; validation material is in the final subsection.
Reports computations for DM and VTR functionals and compares published bounds.

sections.id: Section VII, Discussion and Open Problems
sections.coverage: Discusses tighter run-length functionals, search, run-length constellations, and extensions to other channels.
Summarizes the paper’s contributions and limits.
Lists cited works; the PDF has no appendices.
Motivates a unified cluster-expansion criterion for continuous/discrete models and correlation functions.
Defines the measure-space partition function, connected-cluster coefficients, Theorem 1 hypotheses, and rooted absolute-convergence proof.
States and proves weighted pinned-correlation bounds under the strengthened pointwise integrability hypotheses.

The Section 4 heading and opening sentence appear at the bottom of PDF p. 7; the application examples and derivations begin on p. 8 and continue through p. 10. This distinguishes the heading page from the substantive application pages.
Lists cited works.
Introduces abstract hard-core polymer models, the Penrose tree identity, and the paper’s improved convergence criterion.

sections.id: Section 2, Polymer Models and Classical Criteria
sections.coverage: Defines the partition function and rooted cluster series, recalls Dobrushin/Kotecký–Preiss criteria, and sets up the neighborhood polynomial.
§3.1 states new criteria and §3.2 compares them with prior tests and examples.

The rendered PDF shows the Section 4 heading on physical p. 10 (printed p. 10); §4.1 proves the partitionability/Penrose identity, and §4.2 establishes tree bounds, convergence, and monotone iteration.
Lists cited works; the paper has no appendices.
Defines the interaction norm with its 1/k! and distinct nonzero tuples, establishes entropy regularity, and proves the Gibbs pressure variational identity.
Proves uniqueness/extremality only under the source’s generic interaction condition.
Defines Gibbs-point-process/polymer activity expansions and states necessary/sufficient criteria with their potential assumptions.
Derives recursive Kirkwood–Salsburg/graph bounds and proves the main convergence criteria.
Works through hard-core polymer applications and supporting arguments; necessity remains restricted to the repulsive model as stated.
States the virial-coefficient majorant and derives the radius bound via Lagrange inversion.
Proves the coefficient estimates and compares two model-specific cluster bounds under stability/temperedness assumptions.
Explains the Shearer, independent-set polynomial, hard-core gas, and cluster-expansion links.
Proves the improved Lovász local lemma from the stated cluster criterion and gives a lopsided variant.
Applies the event/dependency-graph theorem to transversals and k-SAT.
Proves the partition-function implication through positive series/fixed-point majorants and lists references.
Reviews polling models and proved large-switch-over results under Poisson or branching-type assumptions.
States the general-renewal conjecture/open problem, explains a heuristic, and reports phase-type numerics.
Defines regenerative cycles and states the renewal-reward theorem with absolute cycle-integrability.
Covers delayed/stationary regenerative variants and their separate initial-delay/length-bias conditions.
Covers point processes, renewal processes, forward recurrence and equilibrium distribution, backward recurrence, spread, inspection paradox, implications, and examples in §§1.1–1.9.
§2.1 states and proves Theorem 2.1 under i.i.d. cycle pairs and integrable reward, using cycle-count bounds and uniform integrability; §2.2 gives examples.
Identifies arXiv v1, authors, date and the upper/lower bound contributions.
Lists sections and physical-page start locations.
Defines the binary i.i.d. deletion channel, reviews prior bounds, states Theorem 1.1 on physical PDF p. 4 and Theorem 1.2 on p. 5, and gives the proof roadmap.
Reviews finite DMC capacity and Blahut–Arimoto; derives fixed-length and uniformly selected-subsequence auxiliary deletion channels and their capacity comparison.
Uses caching, loop-nest optimization, symmetry and sparse transitions; reports finite-channel numerical upper bounds.
States the rigorous run-length construction and its bound under the source’s admissible run-law conditions.
Defines an approximate rate score and describes the practical outer basin-hopping search over parameters.
Derives the score heuristically and explicitly lists omitted O(D²) and entropy/ambiguity terms.
Gives the constrained BAA-type algorithm and its approximation lemma for the stated score; this does not certify the outer practical search as a global optimizer of true code rate.
Lists cited sources.
Identifies arXiv v4 and the two insertion models; states the asymptotic contribution.
Motivation, literature, contributions, and organization.
Defines simple and Gallager insertion channels, Dobrushin capacity characterization, stationary-ergodic rate and run-length notation. Theorem 1 and Lemma 2 proofs are referred to prior sources.
Defines input/output run segments and derives the entropy-chain decomposition for mutual information.
Computes the entropy of the insertion-location and inserted-bit process for simple insertion.
Analyzes ambiguity of the insertion pattern and inserted symbols given input, output and output-run lengths.
Bounds output-run-length uncertainty and develops the corresponding entropy estimates.
Bounds output entropy conditional on the input.
Uses i.i.d. Bernoulli(1/2) input for the simple-insertion lower rate.
Truncates run lengths for high-entropy stationary inputs and proves the simple-insertion converse.
Repeats the entropy decomposition, achievability and converse for bit replacement by two fair random bits; Lemma 21 proof is abbreviated by reference to Section IV and prior work.
Summarizes results and possible extensions.
Lists the cited literature.
Motivates large deterministic switch-over analysis and identifies the branching-process context.
Defines cyclic Poisson queues, gated/exhaustive service, deterministic setups and the stability regime.
Defines originators, descendant sets, reference polling epochs and DSA variables.
Derives recursive PGFs and first/second factorial-moment recurrences.
Proves the almost-sure queue-length limit and uniform scaled-delay limit using descendant independence, renewal-reward SLLN and transform relations.
Illustrates the asymptotic law for selected queueing models.
Discusses uniform-law properties and gives a stochastic-switch-over counterexample to the deterministic-setup theorem’s key relation; leaves extensions open.
Acknowledgement and bibliography.
Identifies the Eindhoven SPOR report repository artifact and document version.
Identifies the 6 Dec 2006 report and introduces branching-type polling systems.
Defines Poisson arrivals, service/setup model, Property 2.1 branching replacement PGFs, stability and exhaustiveness.
Defines offspring PGFs and gives exhaustive, gated and binomial policy examples.
Proves large-deterministic-setup delay/queue-length limits, including Theorem 3.3 and policy dependence through exhaustiveness.

sections.id: Section 3.3, General setups under heavy traffic
sections.coverage: Derives the stochastic-setup limit in the ordered regime ρ↑1 followed by mean setup→∞, with finite first two setup moments.
Discusses implications, numerical comparisons and proposed extensions; simulations do not prove renewal-arrival results.
Gives phase-type fitting relations.
Bibliography of the 2006 report.
Introduces Mayer coefficients, classical stable-potential criteria and the tree-graph approach.
Defines a continuous gas with stable and tempered pair potential and prior convergence bounds.
States Theorem 1 coefficient/radius bounds, Proposition 1 tree-graph inequality and the induced virial-radius estimate.
Defines partition schemes and proves the graph-interval identity.
Builds a deterministic MST-based partition scheme and proves the stable-potential tree bound.
Completes the pointwise tree-graph inequality.
Integrates the coefficient estimate, sums the Cayley-tree majorant and obtains uniform Mayer convergence.
Compares bounds and notes special-potential refinements.
Bibliography.

sections.id: Title, abstract, introduction, model, and notation
sections.coverage: Introduces D-repeat/deletion channels, run-length decomposition, contribution, and roadmap.

sections.id: Section 3, Mean-limited channels and convex duality
sections.coverage: Develops the output-law relative-entropy dual, Theorem 1 and equality conditions, and multiple-use extension.
Proves Theorem 4 and Corollary 5 by separating preprocessor/run processor and reducing to mean-limited bounds.
Constructs digamma/dual-feasible distributions, analytic estimates, and Theorems 10 and 17.
Proves binomial mean-limited criteria, inverse-binomial estimates, and truncated-distribution Theorem 34.

sections.id: Section 7, Deletion-channel capacity bounds and discussion
sections.coverage: Combines dual bounds in Theorems 35 and 38, discusses limiting regimes, and lists open questions.
Gives citations, deferred derivations, analytic estimates, numeric illustrations, and explicitly nonrigorous heuristic estimates where stated.

sections.id: Title, abstract, introduction, model, and Lovász local lemma overview
sections.coverage: Motivates the repulsive lattice gas, independent-set polynomial, and event-avoidance criteria.

sections.id: Section 2, Repulsive lattice gas and fundamental theorem
sections.coverage: Defines partition/nonvanishing regions, Mayer coefficients, and proves the equivalent zero-free/log-series criteria in Theorem 2.10.

sections.id: Section 3, Hard-core lattice gas and examples
sections.coverage: Specializes to independent-set polynomials and develops examples, tree recursions, and fugacity bounds.
States and proves the sharp hard-core event criterion Theorem 4.1 and soft-core extension Theorem 4.2.
Compares sufficient conditions and their implications for partition-function zero-freeness.
Gives tree-based interpretations and unfolding arguments for hard-core criteria.

sections.id: Section 8, Infinite-volume limits and fugacity estimates
sections.coverage: Studies infinite graphs/free energy and derives critical-fugacity estimates under the stated graph assumptions.
Lists cited literature.
Defines finite/infinite-volume pressure, density, virial coefficients, stability and the Mayer-integrability/temperedness quantity; states the gas-model scope.
Introduces the density-to-fugacity inversion and coefficient contour formula used to relate cluster coefficients to virial coefficients.

sections.id: §3, Lower bound on the virial radius
sections.coverage: Uses the Penrose cluster-coefficient estimate, the inverse-density relation, and a scalar maximization to derive the finite-volume virial-radius lower bound (Eq. 3.11) and finite-volume virial-coefficient estimate k|β_k(V)| (Eq. 3.13); Eq. 3.14 instead bounds infinite-volume irreducible Mayer cluster integrals k|β_k|, followed by the infinite-volume radius consequence in Eq. 3.15. All four are on physical PDF p. 3 / printed p. 843.

sections.id: §4, Upper bound on the virial radius
sections.coverage: Uses the hard-core maximum density to bound the radius from above.
States the bounded simply-connected-domain regularity hypothesis and applies Vitali convergence to obtain uniform convergence on interior contours.

sections.id: §§6–8, Infinite-volume relation, other densities, and summary
sections.coverage: Relates finite- and infinite-volume radius bounds, extends the coefficient-radius discussion to other density expansions, and summarizes numerical constants and model limits.
Checks final printed page 847 and end matter; the seven-page scan is complete.

sections.id: Title, abstract, introduction, and polymer model
sections.coverage: Defines the abstract hard-core polymer gas, incompatibility, connected multi-indices, and cluster weights.
States the δ/L(δ) activity hypotheses and rooted/unrooted absolute cluster bounds.
Splits the partition function into compatible/incompatible terms and closes the logarithmic cluster bound inductively.
Treats finite-order/partial-polymer forms of the criterion and their proof.
Compares the sufficient criterion with related Dobrushin/Kotecký–Preiss conditions and lists references.
Identifies the deposited article artifact.

sections.id: Article title, introduction, model, assumptions, and Theorems 2.1–2.3
sections.coverage: Defines the measurable pair-potential model, stability and weighted-integrability assumptions, absolute cluster expansion, correlations, and decay statements.

sections.id: Sections III–V, classical gas, polymers, and quantum gas applications
sections.coverage: Checks examples and model-specific sufficient conditions, including Wiener-sausage estimates.
Proves connected-graph to tree-sum bounds using the Ruelle algebra and BBF tree identity/regularization.
Uses tree majorants, induction, connected-graph decomposition, and absolute convergence for the main statements.
Lists cited works.

read_units.coverage: Defines entropy, divergence, mutual and conditional information; proves finite-alphabet entropy-rate limit, upper semicontinuity/affinity and ergodic decomposition with stated integrability; establishes conditional chain rules, Markov-reference relative-entropy-rate formulas, Markov-approximation convergence, and relative-entropy-density one-sided bounds.
Partial channel/stationarity discussion; not counted as a complete selected unit.
